note: The family variable slug, calendar, exists only through the period-family curation. From the scope naming test: a curated period-family name beside native names leaves each native variable its literal provider key, in another register (the fixture's VarId 101 for value) and in the family's own register (VarId 230 for plain), as the replaced test put both names in one register. From the shared-family test: the entry has no `expected_definitions` and every month delivers the same definition (here the fixture's default, 'A generic family label'), so the family forms without a diagnostic, keeps that one definition on the variable and its state, and its month windows carry shared metadata with no definition of their own. The checked family with differing definitions is period-family-months-merge-or-go-stale-per-register.
fails_if: the period-family compile in curation_compile.py stops declaring the family variable slug `calendar` for register 2's month columns, so the relations.toml edge to scb/other/calendar has no target and no same_as rows are built; or `native_provider_keys` (source_naming.py) derives provider keys from non-native naming targets too, so the family's non-R.V source id aborts the build; or `native_provider_keys` stops deriving a key for the native variables of a register that also declares a period family, so plain is withheld instead of published with provider key 230; or an unreviewed family's months get `per_column` windows or lose their common definition to a projection
